sections.title: Article 1 (Purpose)
paragraphs: These Terms govern the use of the ride-tracking and social platform service (including the website and mobile applications) provided by Orider ("Company"), and define the rights, obligations, and responsibilities between the Company and Users, as well as other necessary matters.

sections.title: Article 2 (Definitions)
list: "Service" means all services provided by the Company through the website (orider.app) and mobile applications (Android, iOS), including ride record management, data analysis, segments and leaderboards, social features, and external service integrations.
"User" means a member or non-member who accesses and uses the Service in accordance with these Terms.
"Member" means a person who has signed in via a Google account or similar method and entered into a service agreement with the Company.
"Content" means all information uploaded or posted by Users, including ride records, photos, comments, descriptions, and profile information.
"External Service" means a third-party service such as Strava that the Company integrates with.

sections.title: Article 3 (Formation of Service Agreement)
list: A service agreement is formed when the User agrees to these Terms and completes the sign-in process.

The Company may restrict registration or terminate the agreement after the fact in the following cases: (1) if another person's information is misused, (2) if the User is under 14 years old (including without legal guardian consent), (3) if the User violates laws or these Terms.
Members may not transfer, lend, or share their account with others.

sections.title: Article 4 (Account Management)
list: Members are responsible for managing their own account information.
Members must promptly notify the Company if unauthorized use of their account is suspected.
The Company is not responsible for damages caused by the Member's own fault.

sections.title: Article 5 (Provision and Modification of the Service)
paragraphs: The Company provides the following services:
list: Ride record storage and analysis
Strava data migration and synchronization
Segments and leaderboards
Social features such as friends, comments, and kudos
Real-time ride recording (GPS route, speed, elevation)
BLE sensor integration (heart rate, cadence, power, gearing, radar)
Group rides and real-time location sharing
list2: The Service is currently in an early (Beta) stage and some features may change or be discontinued.
The Company may modify all or part of the Service for operational or technical reasons; significant changes will be announced in advance.
The Service is currently provided free of charge, but paid features may be introduced in the future with prior notice.

sections.title: Article 6 (External Service Integration and Data)
list: The Service may integrate with external services such as the Strava API with the User's explicit consent.
Some features may be limited due to changes in external service policies, API limits, or outages.
The Company does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of data fetched from external services.
Users may disconnect external services at any time, in which case authentication tokens are discarded.
Deleting data from the Service does not affect data on external services.

sections.title: Article 7 (Privacy Protection)
list: The Company processes and protects Users' personal information in accordance with applicable laws.
Categories collected, purposes, and retention periods are governed by the separate Privacy Policy.
Users may export or request deletion of their data through Settings.

sections.title: Article 8 (User Obligations and Prohibited Activities)
paragraphs: Users must not engage in any of the following:
list: Acts that violate laws or these Terms
Infringing on others' rights (copyright, portrait rights, personal data, etc.)
Posting content that defames, insults, or causes hate or discomfort
Mass collection (scraping) using automated tools, generating abnormal traffic
Reverse engineering, bypassing access, sharing credentials, or interfering with Service operation
Inducing violations of external service policies

sections.title: Article 9 (Restriction and Termination of Use)
list: The Company may issue warnings, temporary suspension, or permanent suspension if a User violates these Terms.
For serious violations, use may be restricted without prior notice.
Members may request withdrawal at any time; upon withdrawal, personal data is processed in accordance with applicable laws and the Privacy Policy.
Members may appeal restriction measures to the Company.

sections.title: Article 10 (Content Rights and Liability)
list: Users must own or have lawful rights to the content they upload.
Users grant the Company a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to the extent necessary to provide, display, store, and transmit the Service.
The Company may take temporary measures (blinding, deletion, etc.) on content suspected of infringement.
Users are responsible for any disputes arising from their content.

sections.title: Article 11 (Service Interruption)
list: The Company may temporarily interrupt all or part of the Service due to system maintenance, failures, or force majeure.
Notices will be posted in advance when possible, or after the fact when unavoidable.

sections.title: Article 12 (Limitation of Liability)
list: The Company limits its liability for the free Service to the extent permitted by law.
The Company is not liable for damages caused by external service outages or policy changes.
The Company is not liable for indirect, special, or consequential damages.
However, damages caused by the Company's willful misconduct or gross negligence are governed by applicable laws.

sections.title: Article 13 (Changes to Terms)
list: The Company may change these Terms within the scope permitted by law.
Changes will be announced through the Service screen or by email.
Users who do not agree to the changes may withdraw.

sections.title: Article 14 (Dispute Resolution and Governing Law)

guidelines.intro: Orider is a platform for a healthy riding culture. All Users must comply with the following standards.
highlights: Share ride records and opinions based on facts.
Do not post another person's location, contact details, face, or other personal information without permission.
Record manipulation, ranking manipulation, and hate speech damage community trust.

next.title: After reviewing the guide
next.body: Return home to check your rides, or join the community to share riding experiences. Use contact or report when you see a problematic post or have feedback.

sections.title: 1. Respect and Consideration
items: Do not defame, insult, mock, threaten, or use hate speech toward others.
Do not discriminate or exclude people based on race, gender, age, region, disability, physical condition, ability, or equipment level.
Do not make fun of riding ability or records. Give specific and respectful advice when it is welcome.
Prioritize safety and consideration in group rides, events, posts, and comments.

sections.title: 2. Ride Records and Location Privacy
sections.intro: Because Orider handles movement routes and activity data, location privacy matters more than in a general community.
items: Do not disclose another person's home, workplace, frequent start point, live location, or contact details without permission.
When sharing a group ride route, hide exact start and finish points or places that can identify a participant.
Do not share sensitive data such as heart rate, power, fatigue, injuries, or health status without the rider's consent.
Before posting screenshots, check and hide names, profiles, map coordinates, invite links, API keys, and other identifiers.

sections.title: 3. Safe Content and Riding Culture
items: Do not post violent, obscene, or illegal content.
Do not glorify or encourage dangerous riding, traffic law violations, chasing, threatening riding, or harassment.
When discussing crashes, injuries, or rescue situations, protect the privacy and dignity of the people involved.
Frame training or health comments as personal experience, not as medical diagnosis.

sections.title: 4. Photos, Videos, Portrait Rights, and Copyright
items: Do not post or redistribute another person's photos, videos, ride records, course files, or writing without permission.
Before posting group ride photos, make sure the people shown are comfortable with public sharing.
Commercial promotion, paid coaching, event promotion, and copied external content must make source and permission clear.
Images or records under dispute may be hidden or removed while they are reviewed.

sections.title: 5. Fair Leaderboards and Record Trust
items: Do not manipulate GPS data, falsify records, upload vehicle-assisted activities, or submit abnormal data.
Do not use automation, multiple accounts, or false activities to manipulate rankings or badges.
If you find sensor or recording errors, correct them where possible or avoid using them in public competition.
Repeated suspicious records may be hidden, excluded from leaderboards, or lead to account restrictions.

sections.title: 6. Groups, Events, and Friends
items: Operate groups and events in a way that respects participant safety, time, and privacy.
Do not repeatedly invite people to unwanted groups, events, messages, or friend requests.
For events that include offline meetups, clearly describe difficulty, distance, expected time, equipment, and risks where possible.
Do not use organizer or moderator privileges to unfairly exclude or harass users.

sections.title: 7. Creator, Recipes, and Share Cards
sections.intro: Content built with Creator Hub or the Personal Data API must be especially clear about data exposure.
items: Recipes, automations, and share cards should clearly explain required scopes and what data is made visible.
Do not post API keys, auth tokens, webhook URLs, personal emails, or raw private activity data in posts or comments.
Prefer aggregate values and safe summaries in share cards. Hide precise routes, start locations, and sensitive metrics by default.
Recipes that fetch or send another person's data without permission are not allowed.

sections.title: 8. Reports, Review, and Appeals
items: Use contact or report for privacy exposure, harassment, record manipulation, illegal content, or safety threats.
When reporting, include the relevant post, comment, record, user, and situation as specifically as possible.
Orider may temporarily hide content or request more information while reviewing a report.
If you believe an enforcement action was incorrect, you may appeal through the contact channel.

sections.title: 9. Enforcement Policy
sections.intro: Depending on severity, repetition, and potential harm, violations may result in:
items: Guidance or warning
Content hiding or removal
Leaderboard exclusion or record invalidation
Temporary suspension or feature restriction
Permanent suspension for serious or repeated violations
sections.footer: Serious violations that threaten safety or expose private information may be restricted immediately without prior warning.

privacy.title: Orider Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Orider ("Company") complies with the Personal Information Protection Act and other applicable laws and establishes and discloses this Privacy Policy as follows to protect Users' personal information.

sections.title: Article 1 (Personal Information Collected)
paragraphs: The Company collects the following personal information:

groups.heading: 1. Sign-up and sign-in
list: Google account information: name, email address, profile image
Google unique identifier
When Naver or Kakao sign-in is selected: the provider-specific user ID, nickname and profile image if consented to and provided
Naver/Kakao connection maintenance and revocation: OAuth access/refresh tokens and expiry information (server only)

groups.heading: 2. Strava integration
list: Strava unique ID
Ride records (distance, speed, elevation, route, activity time, etc.)
Activity descriptions, segment records, and other data the User has made public on Strava
OAuth access and refresh tokens and expiry information for the connection

groups.heading: 3. Automatically collected during use
list: Access logs, IP address
Device info (device type, OS version)
Cookies (web) and local storage (app)
Location info (GPS): ride and run routes, real-time location sharing
BLE sensor data: heart rate, cadence, power, gearing status, radar
SDK usage data: screen views, app interactions, sessions and performance, crash reports and error diagnostics
App and installation identifiers, user identifiers associated with the signed-in account, and push notification tokens
Approximate location, such as country or city, derived from IP addresses. Google Analytics uses IP addresses to derive location but does not log or store the IP addresses themselves.

groups.heading: 4. Additional collection on mobile apps
list: Device identifiers (device model, OS version, app version)
Bluetooth device info (connected sensor name, device ID)
Background location (during ride recording, with User consent)
When using the Wear OS watch app: workout data measured by the watch during exercise, including heart rate, GPS location, distance, speed, cadence and altitude

sections.title: Article 2 (Purposes of Collection and Use)
paragraphs: The Company processes personal information for the following purposes:
list: Member identification and account management
Storing and analyzing ride and run records
Providing Strava integration features
Operating leaderboards and social features
Collecting real-time ride and sensor data
Real-time location sharing during group rides
BLE sensor integration and device management
Service improvement and error analysis
Compliance with laws and dispute response

sections.title: Article 3 (Retention and Use Period)
list: Account deletion requests are processed by a server job in stages, with failed steps retried.
However, data may be retained for a certain period if required by applicable laws.

Request deletion of your account and active service data on the account deletion page. Raw-archive verification requires at least 24 hours. That page describes separate provider processing and retention of error logs, recovery copies, existing backups and minimal technical status. Active-account deletion completion does not confirm erasure of every provider or backup copy.

sections.title: Article 4 (Provision to Third Parties)
paragraphs: The Service processes data with the external providers described in this Policy. Processing on behalf of O-Rider differs from processing independently determined by an external provider for its own purposes. See the Mapbox section below for information sent with map requests and its processing scope.
list: When the User has consented in advance
When required by law
sections.footer: Strava integration uses your choice and OAuth authorization. Features you request, such as workout uploads, transmit the relevant workout data to Strava under its separate policies.

sections.title: Article 4-2 (Data Processing for Strava Integration)
paragraphs: When a User integrates a Strava account, data is processed as follows:

groups.heading: 1. Data collected
list: Strava profile info (name, profile image)
Ride activity summary (distance, speed, heart rate, power, cadence, elevation)
GPS route data (lat/lng, elevation profile)
Segment records and achievements (PR, KOM)
Activity photos (if selected by the User)

groups.heading: 2. Purposes of use
list: Unified management and analysis of the User's ride records
Visualization features such as elevation profiles and performance charts
Segment leaderboards and personal record comparison

groups.heading: 3. Data access scope (OAuth scopes)
list: read — Read public profile information
activity:read_all — Read all activity data
activity:write — Upload activities from mobile apps and publish activity share summaries from the web

groups.heading: 4. Withdrawal of consent and data deletion
list: Users may disconnect Strava integration at any time from the Settings page.
Strava authentication tokens are discarded immediately upon disconnection.
Users may request deletion of all activity data imported from Strava from the Settings page.
Strava data cleanup is separate from O-Rider account deletion. To delete your account, workouts and photos, use the account deletion page and check the server-confirmed completion status.

groups.heading: 5. Credential security
list: Strava OAuth tokens are processed on the server for integration features. The authenticated account’s app may also download, store and synchronize them on the device. Tokens are credentials and are not made public to other users.
Token exchange is handled over HTTPS encrypted communication.

sections.stravaLinkSentencePrefix: Data processing on the Strava platform follows the
sections.stravaLinkSentenceSuffix: . If this Policy and the Strava policy conflict, the Strava policy shall prevail.

sections.title: Article 4-3 (Health Platform Integration and Health Data)
paragraphs: When you connect a device health platform such as Apple Health (HealthKit), Health Connect (Android) or Samsung Health in the mobile app, we process data as follows.

Health data is sensitive information under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, so we obtain separate consent, distinct from general privacy consent, before collection. Core features such as ride recording remain fully available if you decline.

groups.heading: 1. Data collected (only items you consent to)
list: Workout records — activity type, start and end time, distance, calories, heart-rate samples and statistics recorded during the workout
Workout routes — GPS locations recorded during the workout (latitude, longitude, altitude, timestamp, accuracy)
Recovery data (with additional consent) — heart-rate variability (HRV), resting heart rate, sleep duration

groups.heading: 2. Purpose of use
list: Creating and analyzing service activities, such as route maps and segment efforts, from workouts recorded on your watch or device
Recovery (readiness) analysis and training intensity guidance
If you enable it, recording rides completed in O-Rider to Apple Health as workouts (distance, calories, heart rate)

groups.heading: 3. Retention and deletion
list: Imported activities are retained until you delete them individually or delete your account.
Deleting an activity also deletes data derived from it.

groups.heading: 4. Withdrawal of consent
list: You can disconnect anytime in the app under Settings > Health Sync; collection stops immediately.
Health platform access can also be revoked per item in each platform's settings (iOS Settings > Health, Android Health Connect, the Samsung Health app).

groups.heading: 5. Processing principles
list: Health data is used for service features and not for advertising. User-requested integrations and processing by the service providers described in Article 5 may apply.
Data in transit and at rest is protected by HTTPS and access controls.

sections.title: Article 4-4 (Naver/Kakao sign-in and account connections)
paragraphs: When you choose Naver or Kakao sign-in, we use the provider-specific user ID to create an account or let you explicitly connect it to your existing signed-in account. Matching email addresses do not automatically merge accounts. We do not require a separate service password.

groups.heading: 1. Purposes and optional profile information
list: Provider-specific user IDs support sign-in, account identification and connection management.
If consented to and provided, nicknames and profile images are used in your service profile. You can sign in without them and edit your profile in Settings > Account.

groups.heading: 2. Credential retention and disconnection
list: OAuth access/refresh tokens and expiry information are retained in access-restricted server-only storage to maintain and revoke provider connections. They are not sent to the browser.

Request disconnection in Settings > Account > Sign-in connections. The connection mapping and credentials are removed after provider revocation succeeds. Failed revocation is not shown as complete and can be retried.
The last remaining sign-in connection cannot be removed. Connect another sign-in method first or request account deletion.

Disconnecting a sign-in provider does not delete your O-Rider account. You can rename your nickname and change or remove your profile image in settings. To delete the full account and profile, request account deletion.

groups.heading: 3. Account deletion
list: Request full account deletion on the account deletion page. The server processes deletion, including Naver/Kakao provider revocation, in sequence and retries failures. Check processing and completion status on that page.

sections.title: Article 5 (External Providers and Processing)
paragraphs: We use Google LLC services, including Firebase and Google Cloud, for authentication, data storage, server operations and notifications, and Google Analytics and Firebase Crashlytics for usage, error and performance analysis. The information below is transmitted to and processed by Google.

Firebase customer data is processed on our behalf under the applicable processing terms. Google Analytics has separate terms, and service data Google processes for its own operations and security may follow separate policies. Not all Google processing has the same provider role.

groups.heading: 1. Authentication, storage and service operations
list: Firebase Authentication: account identifiers, email and profile, authentication and connection information — sign-in, account management and abuse prevention

Cloud Firestore, Realtime Database, Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions and Hosting: service data you store or transmit, including account, workout, route, sensor and photo data, and request information — synchronization, storage, analysis features and web/server operations
Firebase Cloud Messaging and App Check: app/installation identifiers, notification tokens and app/device attestation information — notification delivery and access protection

groups.heading: 2. Usage analysis and reliability
list: Google Analytics: screen views, interactions, sessions, app/device/installation and account-associated identifiers, and IP-derived approximate location — usage analysis and feature improvement

Firebase Crashlytics: crash/error records, app/device information and installation identifiers — troubleshooting and reliability. SDKs may automatically collect and transmit some information while the app is used.

sections.title: Article 6 (User Rights and How to Exercise Them)
paragraphs: Users may exercise the following rights at any time:
list: Request to view personal information
Request to correct personal information
Request to delete personal information
Request to download data (ZIP)
sections.footer: Rights may be exercised by email, and the Company will act without delay.

sections.title: Article 7 (Cookies and Similar Technologies)
paragraphs: The Service uses cookies and device storage to maintain sign-in and preferences. Browser settings can restrict storage, which may affect some features. Blocking browser storage alone does not stop app SDK analytics or diagnostic collection. Contact the privacy officer listed in this Policy with requests about data processing or collection.

sections.title: Article 8 (Security Measures)
paragraphs: The Company implements the following protective measures:
list: OAuth-based authentication
HTTPS encrypted communication
Minimization of access permissions
Internal access log management

sections.title: Article 9 (Protection of Children's Information)
paragraphs: Children under the age of 14 may not register without the consent of a legal guardian.

sections.title: Article 10 (Privacy Officer)
list: Email: orider.app@gmail.com

sections.title: Article 11 (Changes to the Policy)
paragraphs: This Policy may be revised due to changes in laws or the Service, and changes will be announced.

mapbox.title: Data processing by Mapbox map services
mapbox.body: To display maps, O-Rider requests map tiles and styles from Mapbox over HTTPS. These requests may transmit your IP address, device and app request information, and the requested map area. When the map follows your current location, tile areas can reveal the neighborhood of your actual location. Panning elsewhere may request an area different from your current location. Mapbox normally retains IP addresses for 30 days to provide services, bill customers and maintain security, with longer retention possible for investigations. Mapbox independently determines some processing for its own purposes, which follows its own privacy policy.

accountDeletion.title: Delete your O-Rider account and data
accountDeletion.intro: Request deletion of your O-Rider account here without reinstalling the app. This applies to the same account used on the phone app and Wear OS watch.
accountDeletion.scope: This permanent request removes your active O-Rider sign-in account, profile, workouts and GPS routes, heart rate and sensor data, photos, analysis and coaching history, connection tokens and linked service data. Provider-held data and backup copies follow the separate retention and deletion information below. Export records you need first.
accountDeletion.retention: The server processes deletion in stages and retries failed steps. Service access may be restricted during processing. Residual raw-archive verification requires at least 24 hours and may take longer with retries. Minimal technical status (account identifier, processing phase and timestamps) is retained for completion checks, recovery and prevention of data reappearance. A request receipt is stored in this browser session so progress remains available after sign-in ends.
accountDeletion.thirdParty: Data already sent to services such as Strava must be deleted separately under their policies. Deleting O-Rider does not delete your account at those services.
accountDeletion.steps: 1. Sign in to the O-Rider account you want to delete. 2. Read the scope and type DELETE. 3. Select the deletion request button. If recent sign-in is required, verify your identity and submit again.
accountDeletion.signInHelp: If you registered with Google, Naver or Kakao, sign in the same way you registered. For Apple sign-in, guest accounts or sign-in problems, request deletion by email using the contact above. Do not create or link a different Google account. If sign-in is blocked in the in-app browser, open this address in Chrome or Safari.
accountDeletion.confirm: Type DELETE to request permanent deletion.
accountDeletion.submit: Request permanent account and data deletion
accountDeletion.statusFailed: Deletion status could not be verified. Completion has not been confirmed. Check the status again.
accountDeletion.requestFailed: The deletion request could not be confirmed. It has not been marked complete. Check status before submitting again.
accountDeletion.reauthRequired: A recent sign-in is required to verify your identity. Verify again, then select the deletion request button.
accountDeletion.signInFailed: Sign-in or identity verification was not completed. Allow browser popups and try again with the correct account.
accountDeletion.completionNote: A request receipt, sign-out or closed page does not mean active-account cleanup is complete. Completion requires server confirmation of first-party cleanup; provider processing and backup retention remain separate.

state.pending: Deletion request received. Deletion is not complete yet.
state.processing: Your account and data are being deleted. You can check progress on this page.
state.retrying: Some deletion steps have not finished. The server is retrying; deletion is not complete.
state.complete: Cleanup of your active O-Rider account and first-party service data is complete. Provider processing and the log and backup retention described above remain separate.

accountDeletion.support: Apple sign-in, guest account or unable to sign in: email the privacy contact to request account deletion. Include the original sign-in method and account email, if available. Do not send passwords or authentication tokens. Identity verification is required, including for guest accounts; the contact will explain the necessary steps.
accountDeletion.sessionUnavailable: Browser storage is unavailable, so progress can be checked only while this tab remains open. The server continues processing your request. If status is unavailable after reloading or closing the tab, contact the email above.
accountDeletion.providerRetention: Google Analytics processing continues after Google accepts a deletion request. Firebase Crashlytics retains crash records and related identifiers for 90 days before starting removal from live and backup systems; this does not mean every copy is gone at day 90. Provider-retained Firebase Authentication copies follow a separate policy. Operational and security error logs have a 30-day expiry policy.
accountDeletion.backupRetention: Recovery copies of objects deleted from primary storage are retained for 7 days. Some existing activity backups currently have no automatic expiry and require separate cleanup and verification. Completion of active-account deletion does not mean every backup copy has been physically erased. Contact the privacy officer above about deletion of retained copies.
accountDeletion.providerPolicy: Firebase provider retention and deletion policy
accountDeletion.providerProcessing: Google Analytics has accepted the deletion request. Provider-side processing continues; physical erasure has not been confirmed.
accountDeletion.ownerLoginRequired: This sign-in session cannot request account deletion. Verify with the original account rather than a delegated, watch-link or guest session. For an existing Google account, verify again and submit. For Apple or guest accounts, use the email above to arrange identity verification.
